scope: Selected EarlGrey subsystem; the reduced wrapper is a benchmark design choice, not an upstream native top-level. External boundaries do not become DUT RTL targets.
design_choices: Implement one SPI_DEVICE, SPI_HOST0 and USBDEV subsystem. SPI_HOST1 is outside the case.

Preserve source-defined CSR fields and configured geometry; use the authored digital clock/reset/ABI convention in cadence_contract.md. Reduced counts/widths form a distinct profile and cannot inherit full-profile coverage.
Boundary models expose controllable latency, withheld acknowledgement, errors and stopped clocks. Permanently-ready tieoffs cannot substantiate startup/low-power scenarios.
Use one shared interface/module graph for RTL and DV planning; runtime sessions receive relevant source shards and durable state handles.
RTL microarchitecture choices may vary; observable specified behavior and declared integration relationships form the acceptance contract.

source_precedence: Benchmark-author policy: explicit declared field names, bit ranges, access types and selected integration configuration govern over obsolete narrative references. This is an authored exercise policy, not an attributed user instruction or a universal upstream priority rule. Conflicts inside HJSON and behavioral ambiguities use the individually named adjudications; no blanket HJSON-wins rule resolves them. Authored decisions supersede only their stated scope. Preserve original source bytes and provenance. Local open obligations gate only affected acceptance claims. Candidate/golden RTL and UVM are not specification authority. No correction is simulation or coverage evidence.
